land.text: the city of Barcelona, conquered by Louis the Pious of Aquitaine in 801

predecessors.note: The page: 'The area was dominated by the Franks after the conquest of Girona (785)'. Infobox status: 'County of the Frankish Empire (801–10th century)'. The Frankish realm of 801 is Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row (462-849), whose dossier records the 801 gain of Barcelona from the Emirate of Córdoba; West Francia (west-franks, from 843) is the overlord after it. (Reviewer eu-12-c, 2026-10-25: slug was west-franks)

successors.note: Infobox 'Disestablished: 1162'. Cliopatria draws the county to 1168 and its Crown of Aragon row from 1169; the Crown of Aragon dossier must carry the land from 1163.

capitals.name: Barcelona
capitals.note: The county's seat is its name-city: conquered in 801, burned by Almanzor in 985 (Borrell II page), where Ramon Berenguer III died in 1131 (Ramon Berenguer III page). The infobox excerpt returned no capital line.

rulers.name: Bera
rulers.note: Infobox '801–820: Berà'. The pages opened leave 820-878 and 911-945 without a dated list.

rulers.name: Wilfred Borrell
rulers.note: 'inherited the county without any interruption and held it from 897 to 911'.

rulers.name: Borrell II
rulers.note: 'count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 945', with his brother Miró from 947; 'died 993'.

rulers.name: Ramon Borrell
rulers.note: 'count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 992'; associated with his father from 988.

rulers.name: Berenguer Ramon I
rulers.note: Succeeded in 1017 under the regency of his mother; Ramon Berenguer I succeeded his father in 1035.

rulers.name: Ramon Berenguer III
rulers.note: 'count of Barcelona, Girona, and Ausona from 1086', sole ruler from 1097 when Berenguer Ramon II was forced into exile. The reigns of his father Ramon Berenguer II and of Berenguer Ramon II (1076-1086) are not dated on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Ramon Berenguer IV
rulers.note: Infobox '1131–1162'; 'Count of Barcelona and Prince of Aragon'.

correction.text: the county round Barcelona (the 898 outline without the Girona part), as a stand-in: the page dates the conquest, not the extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 801-897; Cliopatria starts in 898. The infobox says 'Established: 801' and 'in 801, the city of Barcelona was conquered by King Louis the Pious of Aquitaine'; the infobox has no area and no page opened gives the county's extent before 898. The stand-in is Cliopatria's 898 outline without its Girona part; Girona (878) and Ausona (886) come in by the ledger. Cliopatria's West Franks shape of 850-897 overlaps this land.

correction.text: Barcelona, Girona and Ausona (Osona), the lands of Wilfred Borrell and Sunyer

keyframe_review.note: 898-959, 5,761 km2 (25 cells: Barcelona, Girona, Manresa, Igualada, Vilafranca). The Wilfred the Hairy page: 'Wilfred Borrell and Sunyer are said to have ruled Barcelona, Girona, and Ausona', and Ausona was held from 886; Cliopatria draws the Vic plain inside its Besalú row, not here, so it is added. Urgell joins in 948 (county-of-barcelona_948). The infobox gives no area. The shape holds 898-947.

correction.text: Barcelona, Girona and Ausona with Urgell (Seu d'Urgell, Andorra)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 948-959: 'Borrell II [...] was the count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 945 and count of Urgell from 948' ('In 948, Borrell inherited Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II'). Cliopatria draws Urgell apart (898-959) and joins it to Barcelona only in 960.

correction.text: Barcelona, Girona and Ausona with Urgell

keyframe_review.note: 960 only, 9,045 km2 (38 cells, with the Seu d'Urgell and Andorra): right for the union with Urgell, which lasts 948-991; the Vic plain (Ausona) is added because Cliopatria draws it in its Besalú row.

correction.text: Barcelona, Girona and Ausona with Urgell

keyframe_review.note: 961-969, 5,761 km2: the shape drops Urgell, but Borrell II 'inherited Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II' in 948 and kept it until his death; the union shape of 960 is used.

correction.text: Barcelona, Girona and Ausona with Urgell

keyframe_review.note: 970-989, 9,045 km2: the union with Urgell is right (Borrell II was count of both from 948 to 992; he went to Rome in 970 and Barcelona was sacked under his rule in 985); the Vic plain is added.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 990-991 only; from 992 use county-of-barcelona_992

keyframe_review.note: 990-999, 8,997 km2 (still with the Seu d'Urgell and Andorra): right for 990-991. Ramon Borrell 'was count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 992' and, 'From 988, Borrell's sons Ramon Borrell and Ermengol appear as rulers in a divided territory' (Borrell II page); neither page says in words that Ermengol took Urgell, but Ramon Borrell's title omits it and Cliopatria's 1000 shape has none. Ausona has its own Cliopatria row from 990.

correction.text: Barcelona and Girona after the loss of Urgell

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 992-999: Barcelona and Girona (with Ausona as its own row) without Urgell, the outline Cliopatria gives from 1000.
1000-1002, 6,142 km2: the years of Almanzor's incursions ('Between 1000 and 1002 Ramon had to deal with a number of incursions by Almanzor'); the page gives no loss of land, and the shape is kept.

1003-1027, 5,856 km2: unverified. Ramon Borrell 'counter-attacked in 1003' and made expeditions to the Ebro and Segre in 1015 and 1016, and the page describes repopulation of Segarra, Conca de Barberà and Camp de Tarragona without a date; none of this is dated as a change of extent, so the small step of 1003 is Cliopatria's.

correction.text: Barcelona and Girona under Berenguer Ramon I and Ramon Berenguer I (1003 outline)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1028-1039. Cliopatria has no Barcelona shape here: its 'County of Ribagorza' row grows to 85,501 km2 in 1028 and 171,828 km2 in 1034 and covers Barcelona, Girona and the Seu d'Urgell (Sancho III's hegemony). The County of Barcelona page speaks of 'the regency of Ermessinde (1018-1044)', the Ramon Borrell page has Berenguer Ramon succeed in 1017 under his mother's regency, and Ramon Berenguer I 'was Count of Barcelona in 1035–1076'; no page opened says Sancho III ruled the county. The 1003 outline stands in; the Ribagorza and Navarre dossiers must say whether this was an overlordship.

1040-1055, 6,693 km2 (west edge from 1.45 to 1.06 E): unverified, the page is silent on territorial changes. The Ramon Berenguer I page says he 'conquered part of the County of Empúries' (County of Barcelona page) and was 'the first Catalan count to acquire Carcassonne and Razès' without years; Empúries has its own Cliopatria row.

1056-1084, 6,741 km2: unverified, the page gives no change in 1056. The only dated acquisition is the 1067 caption 'in return for their rights over Carcassonne'; Carcassonne is not in the shape and is not drawn (notes).
1085-1110, 7,460 km2 (+718 km2): unverified; Ramon Berenguer III was 'count of Barcelona, Girona, and Ausona from 1086' and ruled alone from 1097, but no page opened dates the 1085 step.

correction.text: the shape as drawn (Barcelona, Girona, Ausona and Besalú), for 1111-1116

keyframe_review.note: 1111-1125, 9,537 km2 (38 cells, now with Besalú, Olot and Vic): the 2,078 km2 added in 1111 is Besalú, which Ramon Berenguer III 'inherited' in 1111 (the Besalú page: 'In 1111, Bernard died and Barcelona inherited Besalú'). The shape holds 1111-1116; Cerdanya follows in 1117 and Tarragona by 1118.

correction.text: the county with Cerdanya-Berga, the Conca de Barberà and Tarragona, for 1117-1148

keyframe_review.note: 1126-1151, 15,020 km2 (61 cells: now Berga, Puigcerdà, Ripoll, Solsona, Cardona, and the Conca de Barberà round Valls, Cervera, Siurana; Tarragona itself is outside). Cerdanya came in 1117 ('Cerdanya (1117)'), Tarragona was 'captured and rebuilt' by 1118: the shape holds from 1117 to 1148, with Tarragona added. Cliopatria's step is in 1126. The infobox gives no area.

union.text: Tortosa and its district on the lower Ebro

correction.text: the county with Tortosa and the Lleida-Fraga-Mequinenza country, for 1149-1162

keyframe_review.note: 1152-1168, 19,407 km2 (78 cells; adds Lleida, Fraga, Mequinenza, Falset and Móra d'Ebre but not Tortosa): Tortosa surrendered on 30 December 1148 and Lleida capitulated on 24 October (1149), Fraga and Mequinenza in 1149 (Ramon Berenguer IV page). Cliopatria instead draws the Tortosa district in the Taifa of Murcia's 1152 shape (77,869 km2), the Almoravid shape to 1151 and the Taifa of Valencia shape of 1147-1151; Tortosa is added here and must be taken out there. The county ends in 1162, so the shape holds 1149-1162.

region.text: the city of Barcelona, conquered in 801

ledger.note: 801: Louis the Pious of Aquitaine conquers Barcelona and the county is established. 'in 801, the city of Barcelona was conquered by King Louis the Pious of Aquitaine'; infobox 'Established: 801'; 'The first count of Barcelona was Bera (801–820).' The page gives no extent for the first century, so the region is the city and a radius. (Reviewer eu-12-c, 2026-10-25: counterpart was west-franks; West Francia dates from 843, the Kingdom of the Franks row runs to 849 and its dossier records the 801 gain of Barcelona; infobox status 'County of the Frankish Empire (801–10th century)')

878: Wilfred the Hairy becomes count of Barcelona and Girona. 'Count of Urgell (from 870), Cerdanya (from 870), Barcelona (from 878)'; 'Girona (from 878, as Wilfred II)'; 'On 11 September 878, Bernard was dispossessed of all his titles.' The land is the Girona part of Cliopatria's 898 outline; the page gives no boundary.

886: Ausona (Osona) is added to Wilfred's counties. '[...] Ausona (from 886)'; 'In 885, Wilfred designated a Viscount to control the County of Ausona in his absence'. Vic is the stand-in for the county.

region.text: Urgell, with the Seu d'Urgell and Andorra

ledger.note: 948: Borrell II inherits Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II and holds it with Barcelona, Girona and Ausona. 'Borrell II (died 993) was the count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 945 and count of Urgell from 948'; 'In 948, Borrell inherited Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II.' Cliopatria joins the shapes only in 960.

region.text: Urgell, with the Seu d'Urgell and Andorra

ledger.note: 992: Ramon Borrell succeeds as count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona and Urgell passes to his brother Ermengol. 'was count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 992'; 'From 988, Borrell's sons Ramon Borrell and Ermengol appear as rulers in a divided territory' (Borrell II page). Neither page says in words that Ermengol took Urgell; the Ramon Borrell page names Count Ermengol I (d. 1010) and the bishop Sal·la of Urgell.

1111: Barcelona inherits Besalú. 'He inherited the counties of Besalú (1111) and Cerdanya (1117)'; the Besalú page: 'In 1111, Bernard died and Barcelona inherited Besalú'. Vallespir, Fenolledès, Peyrepertuse and Castellnou went to Cerdanya as compensation (Besalú page).

region.text: Provence county, brought by Countess Dolça

ledger.note: 1112: Ramon Berenguer III marries the heiress of Provence and takes the county. 'He also extended his trans- Pyrenean reign by incorporating Provence county through his marriage to Countess Dolça in 1112'; the Ramon Berenguer III page: 'count of Provence in the Holy Roman Empire, from 1112'. A union by marriage, drawn here as a gain; Cliopatria's Barcelona shape never contains Provence.

union.text: Vallespir, Fenouillèdes and Peyrepertuse across the Pyrenees

region.text: Cerdanya, Berga and the trans-Pyrenean districts

ledger.note: 1117: Cerdanya passes to Ramon Berenguer III. 'He inherited the counties of Besalú (1111) and Cerdanya (1117)'. Another page, not cited here, dates the sale to 1118 (see county-of-berga). Cliopatria takes the land over in 1126.

By 1118: Ramon Berenguer III has captured and rebuilt Tarragona. 'By 1118 he had captured and rebuilt Tarragona'; in 1116 he went to Rome 'to petition Pope Paschal II for a crusade to liberate Tarragona'. The page does not name the holder of Tarragona and Cliopatria's Almoravid shape stops short of the city, so the counterpart is 'nobody'.

1131: Provence goes to the younger son. 'Before he died, he gave his five Catalan counties to his eldest son, Ramon Berenguer IV, and Provence to his younger son, Berenguer Ramon' (Ramon Berenguer III died in 1131).

region.text: Tortosa and its district on the lower Ebro

ledger.note: July 1148: the siege of Tortosa begins. 'The siege of Tortosa (1 July – 30 December 1148)'; 'The Genoese and Catalan fleets sailed from Barcelona on 29 June and entered the Ebro on 1 July 1148.'

region.text: Tortosa and its district on the lower Ebro

ledger.note: 30 December 1148: Tortosa surrenders to Ramon Berenguer IV. 'When the forty-day armistice elapsed, after six months of siege, the Tortosans surrendered on 30 December.' Tortosa 'was back in Almoravid hands by 1118'; the page names no Almoravid commander ('Unknown' in the infobox), so the Almoravids are the counterpart on Cliopatria's reading (its Almoravid shape of 1139-1151 and its Valencia shape of 1147-1151 both cover Tortosa).

region.text: Tortosa and its district on the lower Ebro

ledger.note: 30 December 1148: the fighting for Tortosa ends with the surrender.

1149: Lleida, Fraga and Mequinenza fall to Ramon Berenguer IV. 'Fraga, Lleida and Mequinenza fell "the next year" (1149) "after a seven-month siege."' The Tortosa article adds: 'Raymond Berengar IV followed it up with the conquest of Lleida on his own' and 'On 24 October, Lleida capitulated.' The page names no holder of Lleida; the Almoravid shape covers it on Cliopatria's reading.

region.text: Cerdanya and the lands north of the Pyrenees

ledger.note: 1162: Ramon Berenguer IV dies and Cerdanya goes to his son Pere. 'Ramon Berenguer IV died on 6 August 1162'; 'Pere (Peter) received Cerdanya and lands north of the Pyrenees' (undated on the page; the county-of-berga dossier dates Peter's county 1162-1168).

region.text: the county, joined in personal union with Aragon

ledger.note: 1162: the County of Barcelona enters a personal union with the Kingdom of Aragon. 'In 1162, the County of Barcelona entered into a personal union with the Kingdom of Aragon.' The Ramon Berenguer IV page: betrothed to Petronilla on 11 August 1137, Ramiro II 'withdrew from public life on 13 November 1137, leaving his kingdom to Petronilla and Ramon Berenguer', formally married in 1150, Petronilla abdicated in 1164 and her son became Alfonso II. Cliopatria keeps the two realms apart to 1168.

region.text: the county as it stood in 1162

ledger.note: 1162: the county ends as a state of its own. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1162'; its land passes to the Crown of Aragon (Petronilla's abdication in 1164 made her son Alfonso II, Ramon Berenguer IV page).

wars.name: Almanzor's sack of Barcelona (985)
wars.outcome: Barcelona was burned; Borrell II kept the county and, from 988, its effective independence.
wars.note: 'it was under his rule that Barcelona was sacked in 985 by the Muslim leader Almanzor'; 'In 985 Barcelona, then ruled by Borrell II, was attacked and burned by Muslims, led by Almanzor' (County of Barcelona page). No land changed hands.

wars.name: Almanzor's incursions and the counter-attack on Lleida (1000-1003)
wars.outcome: Ramon Borrell weathered the raids; 'Almanzor died in 1002, and seeing an opportunity Ramon counter-attacked in 1003'. The page records no change of land.

wars.name: Catalan expedition to Córdoba (1010)
wars.outcome: Ramon Borrell and his brother Ermengol sacked Córdoba in May 1010 and took part in the battle of Aqbat al-Bakr on 2 June 1010 'on the side of the Muslim rebels'; Ermengol died. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Expeditions to the Ebro and Segre (1015-1016)
belligerents: Muslim lands on the Ebro and Segre (unnamed on the page)
wars.outcome: 'In 1015 and 1016 Ramon made further expeditions to the rivers Ebro and Segre'; the page does not say the campaigns added territory.
wars.note: The page names no opponent and no state; Cliopatria has the Taifa of Tortosa and the Taifa of Zaragoza on these rivers from 1010 and 1015.

wars.name: Almoravid raids on the county (1102)
wars.outcome: Ramon Berenguer III was 'Responding to increased raids into his lands by the Almoravids in 1102'; the page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Pisan-Catalan expedition to Mallorca and Ibiza (1114-1115)
wars.outcome: 'in 1114 and 1115 attacked with Pisa the then-Muslim islands of Mallorca and Ibiza'; the page records no lasting conquest.

wars.name: Tarragona campaign (1116-1118)
belligerents: Muslim holders of Tarragona (unnamed on the page)
wars.outcome: After the 1116 appeal to Rome 'for a crusade to liberate Tarragona', 'By 1118 he had captured and rebuilt Tarragona'.
wars.note: Only one party is named by the page; the holder of Tarragona is not.

wars.name: Siege of Tortosa (1148)

zones.text: Tortosa and its district on the lower Ebro

wars.outcome: Christian victory: Tortosa surrendered on 30 December 1148 after a six-month siege; Genoa kept a third of the walled city and sold it to Ramon Berenguer IV in 1153 for 16,000 maravedíes.

wars.name: Conquest of Lleida, Fraga and Mequinenza (1149)
wars.outcome: Lleida capitulated on 24 October (1149); Fraga and Mequinenza fell the same year after a seven-month siege.
wars.note: The Tortosa article says Lleida was taken 'on his own', without Genoese help or papal approval.

certainty.note: Comital frontiers follow castles and rivers; no treaty or survey line is given. The first described line, the Peace and Truce of 1173 'from Salses to Lleida and Tortosa', falls after the county's end.

notes: IDENTITY. Cliopatria's Wikipedia field for this row reads 'Girona' and its Wikidata id is Q7038; the article used here is 'County of Barcelona' (all the Wikipedia pages cited), and Q7038 is kept as Cliopatria gives it but is probably not the county's id (Wikidata is unreachable). START AND END. The page's infobox gives 801 and 1162; Cliopatria draws 898 to 1168. Keyframes were added for 801-897 (a stand-in outline: the page dates the conquest of the city, not an extent), and the dossier ends in 1162, so the Crown of Aragon dossier must hold the land from 1163 (Cliopatria's Barcelona shape runs to 1168 and its Crown of Aragon row starts in 1169). The 1137 betrothal, Ramiro II's withdrawal, the 1150 marriage and the 1164 accession of Alfonso II are in the 1162 note; no Barcelona shape changes with them. WHAT THE CLIOPATRIA SHAPES ARE (grid test of their cells): the 898 outline is Barcelona, Girona, Manresa, Igualada and Vilafranca without the Vic plain; 960, 970 and 990 add the Seu d'Urgell and Andorra (Urgell, held 948-991); 1111 adds Besalú, Olot and Vic; 1126 adds Cerdanya-Berga and the Conca de Barberà but not Tarragona; 1152 adds Lleida, Fraga, Mequinenza, Falset and Móra but not Tortosa. The Vic plain sits in Cliopatria's Besalú row (898-989) and in the Osona row (990-1110): the Osona dossier must decide whether it is Barcelona's; the pages say the counts of Barcelona held Ausona from 886. OTHER ROWS THAT NEED CORRECTING BY THEIR OWNERS: the Taifa of Murcia 1152 shape (77,869 km2) covers the Tortosa district and the Almoravid 1139-1151 and Taifa of Valencia 1147-1151 shapes cover Tortosa and Lleida; the County of Ribagorza row 1028-1039 covers Barcelona; the West Franks row 850-897 reaches 41.07 N and overlaps the county's first century; the West Franks owner may want a vassal tint for Barcelona 898-987 ('In 988, the reign of the Carolingian dynasty ended'; Borrell II's refusal to swear allegiance 'has been interpreted as the starting point of effective independence', County of Barcelona page): no vassal event is written here because the suzerain records it. NOT DRAWN. Carcassonne and Razès (Ramon Berenguer I 'acquiring the counties of Carcassonne and Razès'; caption 'in return for their rights over Carcassonne in 1067'): the pages give a rights purchase and no extent, and Cliopatria keeps the land elsewhere. Ramon Berenguer I's conquest of 'part of the County of Empúries' and his 'partnering with the counts of Urgell and Pallars' are undated. The 1153 sale of Genoa's third of Tortosa. The Peace and Truce of 1173. THIN SPOTS. Shapes 1000, 1003, 1040, 1056 and 1085 are kept as ok without a page for their small steps. Provence 1112-1131 is a union by marriage drawn as a gain and loss at confidence 2; county-of-provence needs a dossier. The page budget (9) was exceeded by one: the first Tortosa lookup hit a disambiguation page. The County of Besalú page was read for the 1111 inheritance. Gazetteer names needed: Lleida, Fraga, Mequinenza, Vic, Ripoll (places); Cerdanya, Ausona/Osona, Vallespir (regions); circles by coordinates stand in.
